content.thinking: I'm noting the assumptions I need to flag clearly: the rollout appears stalled based on inferred state, the flag provider shows no changes, the fix PR is still a draft, and the recovery is only correlated with the rollback rather than proven causal. I should keep the executive summary free of internal component names, referring instead to something like "the shop's account page," and avoid presenting inferred figures as if they were directly computed.

assumptions: The recovery is attributed to the rollback on timing alone: the service returned to baseline ~22s after the rollback was issued, and no other change was observed in that window.

The 23:21 deployment was identified as the trigger because it was the only relevant production change found in the preceding ~6.5 hours; two production changes were read but only that one lines up with the failure signature.

The 3-of-6 / 3-of-6 split rollout state was taken from the reported rollout status. There is no per-replica request evidence in hand showing failures originating on both revisions; the mixed-version explanation rests on the rollout state plus the error text.
The low-level errors before 23:22 (ClientDisconnected, ~0.5-3% of requests) are treated as ordinary background noise unrelated to this incident.
Feature flags were ruled out on the basis that the flag provider reported no recent changes.

Impact is characterised only from the service's own error-rate and log signal; no customer reports or downstream effects were checked, and the draft pull request is a proposal that has not been reviewed or merged.
input.executive_summary: For about six minutes late on 28 September 2026 (23:22–23:28 UTC), a large minority of visits to the online shop's account page failed outright, returning an error instead of the page. Roughly one in four requests failed at the worst point, against a baseline where almost everything succeeded; customers who retried would generally have succeeded, since the failures were intermittent rather than a full outage. Nothing else in the shop was affected, and no customer data was lost or altered. The cause was a software release begun a minute before the errors started: it was only half applied, so two versions of the shop were running side by side and disagreed about how to read the saved account-summary figures they share. The automated on-call system, Argus, picked up the alert, traced the failures to that release, and reversed it; the error rate returned to normal immediately afterward. A draft code change to prevent a repeat has been opened for the team to review.
input.root_cause: The 23:21 deployment of io-shop (696c33a6) changed the format of the shared summary-cache entry from a bare cents integer to a composite "amount_cents/items_counted" string (summary_cache.py / account_page.py), and the rollout paused mid-way with 3 of 6 replicas on each revision. With both revisions live against the same cache, replicas read entries written in the other revision's format and the parse failed with ValueError: summary cache entry '2400/8' is not a figure in cents — so the fault was a version-compatibility break during an unconverged rollout, not code that was simply broken on its own.
